definition: Showing sustained care, effort, and diligence.
example: Assiduous preparation made the complex hearing manageable.
nuance: Assiduous emphasizes sustained application rather than innate talent.
prompt: An archivist reconstructs a damaged record.
options: Her assiduous research involved months of careful cross-checking.
Her assiduous research consisted of a careless guess.
The assiduous archivist abandoned the task at the first difficulty.
Assiduous research meant that the subject was easy.
reasons: A careless guess lacks effort and care.
Immediate abandonment does not show persistence.
Assiduous describes effort, not task difficulty.

practice.prompt: A gardener tends a vegetable plot through a long, dry summer.
options: Her assiduous watering each dawn kept the tomato vines alive until August.
His assiduous care meant he watered the beans only when he happened to remember.
The assiduous soil in the corner bed turned the hydrangeas a deep blue.
After one assiduous glance at the sky, she left the rain to handle everything.
reasons: Watering faithfully every morning for weeks shows the steady, devoted work the word describes.
Watering only when it comes to mind is haphazard, the reverse of persistent attention.
This mixes the word up with acidic; soil chemistry involves no effort or care.
A single quick look is a passing act, not long and persistent effort.
